summary: Create Windows private files with a protected owner-only DACL instead of inheriting parent permissions.
reason: The shared generated writer uses chmod, which does not establish a Windows DACL. Parent grants such as CodexSandboxUsers cause the pre-write validator to reject otherwise successful browser logins. This shared writer defect should be upstreamed to Printing Press; the downstream guard records the required Windows behavior until regeneration includes it.
validated_outcome: Synthetic Windows credentials must save beneath a parent with inherited non-owner read grants while the resulting file passes the unchanged owner/DACL validator. A protected DACL is supplied at creation before private bytes are written; CREATE_NEW rejects collisions. POSIX temp creation and the fail-closed pre-write verifier remain intact. Real authentication is user-owned.
